1. The appeal questions dismissal of the Claim Application No.OA/(IIu)/NGP/122/2018 by the Railway Claims 2 fa228.25.odt Tribunal, Nagpur Bench, Nagpur (for short "Tribunal") filed by the appellants for compensation on account of the death of deceased Dalpat Singh, who died in a railway accident on 14.06.2017.

1 2.

The appellants filed a claim application alleging that deceased Dalpat Singh, while boarding the train on 14.06.2017 from Gondia, fell down, sustained injuries and thereafter, succumbed to the injuries.

3. The Railway authority came-up with a case that since the deceased fell while boarding the train,
the said accident is not an untoward incident within the meaning of Section 123(c) read with Section 124-A of the Railways Act.

After considering the submissions, the Tribunal held that no ticket was recovered at the time of preparation of spot panchanama and inquest panchanama and therefore, he was was not a bonafide passenger.
The Tribunal has further held that since the deceased tried to board a running train at Gondia Railway Station, it was criminal negligence and rejected the claim by dismissing the application.

4. Having heard the learned counsels for the parties and having gone through the impugned award,
it transpires that the deceased was intending to travel from Gondia to Wadsa in Train No.78820 (Gondia - Ballarshah Demu Passenger Train).
It has also 3 fa228.25.odt come in the evidence of the guard of the said train that after the train passed half of the platform, there was Alarm Chain Pulling (ACP).
When he alighted from the train, he saw a person lying in an injured condition between the gap of the train and the platform.
The injured was taken to the hospital.

The record of the proceedings reveal that the authority, at page no.A-39 requested to verify Ticket No.UXA-55140327 dated 14.06.2017, which was issued by the Booking Office, South Eastern Railway, Gondia.
On the same letter, an endorsement was made by the Chief Booking Supervisor mentioning that it was issued by Jan Sadharan Ticket Seva Kendra.
The ticket is also part of the record at page no.A-41.
Inspite of this material available on record, the Tribunal erroneously held that the deceased was not a bonafide passenger.
5. This takes me to the submissions with regard to the question whether it was an untoward incident.
Both the learned counsels submitted contrary to each other as to whether falling while boarding the train would be covered within the meaning of "untoward incident".

Without going into detail, it will be sufficient to refer the decision of Union of India Vs. Prabhakaran Vijaya Kumar &
Ors 1 wherein, in para 10 it has been held as under:
1 (2008) 9 SCC 527 4 fa228.25.odt "10.

entities.text:
Union of India Vs. Prabhakaran Vijaya Kumar &
Ors 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: We are of the opinion that it will not legally make any difference whether the deceased was actually inside the train when she fell down or whether she was only trying to get into the train when she fell down.
In our opinion in either case it amounts to an 'accidental falling of a passenger from a train carrying passengers'.

Hence, it is an 'untoward incident' as defined in Section 123(c)
of the Railways Act."
6.

Reference can also be made to the decision of Union of India Vs. Rina Devi 1 wherein the Supreme Court has held that death or injury in the course of boarding or de-boarding a train will be an 'untoward incident' entitling a victim to compensation.

entities.text: Union of India Vs. Rina Devi 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A reference can also be made to the decision in the Jameela and others Vs. Union of India 2 wherein, the Supreme Court in para 9 has held as under:

2 "9.

The manner in which the accident is sought to be reconstructed by the Railway,
the deceased was standing at the open door of the train compartment from where he fell down, is called by the railway itself as negligence.
Now negligence of this kind which is not very uncommon on Indian trains is not the same thing as a criminal act mentioned in clause (c) to the proviso to section 124 A.
A criminal act envisaged under clause (c) must have an element of malicious intent or mens rea.
Standing at the open doors of the compartment of a running train may be a negligent act, even a rash act but, without anything else, it is certainly not a criminal act.

Thus, the case of the 1 AIR 2018 SC 2362 2 AIR 2010 SC 3705 5 fa228.25.odt railway must fail even after assuming everything in its favour."
7.

entities.text: AIR 2018 SC 2362 2 AIR 2010 SC 3705 5 fa228.25.odt railway
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Coming to the point of criminal negligence on the part of the deceased, the Supreme Court in the case of Rina Devi (supra) has held as under:
"25. ...........

We may in this connection refer to judgment of this Court in United India Insurance Co. Ltd. versus Sunil Kumar [2017 (13) SCALE 652] laying down that plea of negligence of the victim cannot be allowed in claim based on 'no fault theory'
under Section 163A of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

entities.text: United India Insurance Co. Ltd. versus Sunil Kumar [2017 (13) SCALE 652]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Accordingly, we hold that death or injury in the course of boarding or de-boarding a train will be an 'untoward incident' entitling a victim to the compensation and will not fall under the proviso to Section 124A merely on the plea of negligence of the victim as a contributing factor"
8.

In view of the above legal position, at the most the act of the deceased while boarding the moving train may be an act of negligence but cannot be said to be a criminal act which requires intention or mens rea, which is not the case of the respondent.
Therefore, the findings recorded by the Tribunal are required to be set aside.
Accordingly, the appeal succeeds.
9. The appeal is allowed.
The respondent is liable to pay compensation of 8,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 6 per cent per annum.

The respondent is directed to credit the amount of 4,00,000/- in the account of appellant no.1 and 1,00,000/- each by way of Fixed Deposit in any nationalized Bank in the name of appellant nos.2 to 4 till they attain the age of majority and the remaining amount of 1,00,000/-
be given to the mother of the deceased, with proportionate interest thereon.
With this, the appeal stands disposed of.
